message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze this situation.

Position: Rhea Lend (ex-Burrow) on NEAR, supplies native USDC (~$1,000), no debt. So it's a supplier position, not a borrower. Risk is mainly about venue solvency, withdrawal availability, oracle issues affecting collateral (bad debt risk for suppliers), utilization/liquidity.

Observations:
- O01 (onchain, 2026-10-20 00:00 UTC): USDC utilization 84.71%, supplied 12.35M, borrowed 10.63M, ledger-available 1.919M, USDC held 1.938M; can_withdraw=true; contract_mode Running. Utilization ~85% is somewhat elevated but there's ~$1.9M available, and user's position is only $1,000. Withdrawals are possible. This is normal-ish for a money market; 85% utilization is high-ish but not alarming; available liquidity far exceeds user's position.
- O02 (official_x, rhea_finance): marketing post about holding stablecoins on HotDAO earning up to 12% APY. This is marketing noise, not risk. Though promoting yield elsewhere... not a risk signal per se. It's just marketing.
- O03 (governance): HSP-029 proposal live and being voted on House of Stake. No details on what it is; no indication it affects Burrow/Rhea. Noise.
- O04 (news): NEAR launches NEAR Business multisig treasury. General ecosystem news, not risk.
- O05 (news): NEAR Intents volume doubles; Q3 $10.41B. Positive ecosystem news, not risk.

No exploit, no oracle fault, no pause, no liquidity run. Contract mode Running, can_withdraw=true. User has no debt, so no liquidation risk. Utilization 84.71% is elevated-ish but liquidity available ($1.9M) is ~1900x the user's position.

Similar past cases are Morpho borrowers with wstETH/USDC — not really relevant (different venue, borrower positions). They survived; no liquidation. Not very informative but suggest no panic.

Risk: low. Action: hold.

Wait — should utilization ~85% push to "elevated"? For a supplier with no debt, high utilization means higher borrow yield (good) but reduced exit liquidity. Available $1.919M vs $1,000 position — trivial. Utilization 84.71% is high but within normal operating range for stablecoin markets; can_withdraw=true. I'd say low risk, hold. Maybe "elevated" with hold? The rubric: exiting without need costs. Nothing indicates an incident. I'll go low, hold.

Reasons: no adverse signals; contract running, withdrawals enabled; liquidity available far exceeds position; user has no debt so no liquidation risk; other observations are marketing/ecosystem noise not touching this venue.

Source IDs: O01 primarily. Maybe include O01 only. The decision is driven by O01 (healthy onchain state) and absence of incident signals in O02-O05. I'll list O01.
